meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (4MA1_1F_2306). Derived metadata only. No exam question text transcribed.

coding_notes: q19(a) is the FIRST sighting of translations in the corpus, and it vindicates putting it back at iGCSE Foundation. It had been moved to Higher on 2026-10-08 purely because vectors was its only prerequisite and vectors is Higher on 4MA1 — a compromise forced by the graph, not by evidence. Scoping prerequisites per course removed the need for it, and this question confirms the restoration was right: translations is Foundation content on 4MA1, as spec 5.2 says.
q9 is a NUMBER MACHINE, the second sighting after Nov23 2F q10, further confirming that excluding function_machines from the iGCSE courses was wrong.

q14(b) is the FIRST genuine sighting of significant_figures. Across the previous fifteen papers the phrase appeared only as an instruction ('give your answer to 3 significant figures'), where the lowest-skill rule puts the tag on the skill being tested. Here rounding a previous answer to 3sf IS the question, so the tag is honest. Bucket C of the three-causes-of-zero-evidence analysis, now resolved.
q23(a) is the first sighting of prime_factor_decomposition.

q15 tagged venn_diagrams, not set_notation: the student completes an actual Venn diagram from two sets given by rule. set_notation covers the symbols and listing members; this is the diagram. Same distinction as Jun24 2F q15 against Jun24 1F q22.
q19(b) is an ENLARGEMENT per the mark scheme, and (c) is a 90 degree clockwise rotation about a given centre.
